lesson_title: You Are Built Like a Building
hook_text: The building next door went up the same way you grew: frame first.
clip_script: A building site in Durban. First: steel columns and beams, joined into a frame, with triangles to keep it stiff. Then: walls and windows to cover it. Now look at you. Bones are the columns and beams. Joints join them. Muscles and skin are the walls. A vertebrate skeleton is a frame structure: strong, light and covered up. Build one with straws and pipe cleaners. Too-thin legs? It sags. Get the frame right, and it stands.
visual_style: Whiteboard building frame that morphs into a dog skeleton made of straws.
mood: Clever and surprising, like a magic trick explained.
pacing: Building frame, then the body as a frame, then a quick model build with one fail and one success.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build a straw skeleton of your favourite animal.
